morph_chan_vese — SEGMENTATION contour op

• Data kinds: image2d × mask → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.morph_chan_vese(image, init, *, n_iter: 'int' = 100, smoothing: 'int' = 1, lambda1: 'float' = 1.0, lambda2: 'float' = 1.0, phase: 'int' = 0, record_every: 'int' = 0) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import segcontour; segcontour.morph_chan_vese(image, init, *, n_iter: 'int' = 100, smoothing: 'int' = 1, lambda1: 'float' = 1.0, lambda2: 'float' = 1.0, phase: 'int' = 0, record_every: 'int' = 0) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("morph_chan_vese"))

Usage

Morphological Chan–Vese (MorphACWE of Márquez-Neila–Baumela–Álvarez 2014). One iteration = data step + smoothing step (morph_chan_vese).

Data stage: c1 = inside mean, c0 = outside mean, aux = |∇u|(λ1 (I − c1)² − λ2 (I − c0)²); pixels with aux < 0 go inside, aux > 0 outside (|∇u| ≠ 0 = only pixels near the boundary move). Smoothing stage: the curvature operator (alternating SI∘IS and IS∘SI) smoothing times. phase = the operator used first (0 = SI∘IS). skimage's implementation keeps the alternating phase in module-global state, so the same input can give a different result depending on the previous call — here every call starts from phase (deterministic). The fitting energy E_fit = λ1 Σ_in (I − c1)² + λ2 Σ_out (I − c0)² is recorded before and after each stage. Gate (exact): with c fixed, E_fit is a per-pixel sum, so every pixel flipped in the data stage lowers E_fit (or leaves it equal), and updating c to the means afterwards lowers it further ⇒ E_fit is monotonically non-increasing across the data stage (n_data_increase = 0). The smoothing stage can raise E_fit (measured in fit_after_smooth).

Returns: mask, fit_before_data / fit_after_data / fit_after_smooth (per iteration), n_data_increase, history, n_iter, n_changed (number of pixels changed per iteration).
